A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 4K4DGen research. All text, equations, tables and figures are readable, including v3's Appendices A–E. v1 ends with references and contains no appendix.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original quantitative comparisons, user-study outcomes, generated examples and ablations on 16 panoramas.

after.justification: Section 4 reports original FID, KID, Q-Align, user-study and ablation results. Appendix D provides additional visual results and detailed vote counts.

M1.justification: The spherical project-denoise-fuse procedure, geometry alignment, time-dependent Gaussian representation and training losses are retained. Dynamic Panoramic Lifting renames the existing lifting component; Appendix C documents its implementation without establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate panorama-to-4D generation using 16 generated panoramas. Appendix B newly identifies SUN360 as the panorama generator's fine-tuning source, clarifying provenance without establishing additional training or evaluation coverage. The extra visual examples remain within the existing task.

E2.justification: 3D-Cinemagraphy remains the external comparison method, and the same animation and lifting variants are evaluated. v3 separately reports its circle and zoom-in configurations; this expands the reported settings rather than introducing another comparison method.

E3.justification: The principal evaluation changes from CLIP consistency and CLIP-I to FID, KID and Q-Align image-quality, aesthetics and video-quality scores. Table 2 also replaces CLIP with Q-Align video quality. v3 explicitly evaluates both baseline motion modes, while retaining the 16-panorama dataset and test-camera disturbance.

E4.justification: Table 2 revises the evidence for the animation-strategy ablation by assessing video quality with Q-Align instead of CLIP. The tested alternatives, motion and view-consistency assessments, and qualitative STA/temporal-loss removal studies otherwise remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. Appendix D.1 adds participant and vote totals, clarifying the existing percentage calculations without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the CLIP results with new quality measurements, including FID 16.59 for 4K4DGen versus 57.05 for zoom-in and 57.78 for circle. Table 2 replaces CLIP scores with Q-Align scores of 0.82/0.64/0.85 for panorama/perspective/ours. Motion scores, 33%/70% consistency votes and 81% preference for 4K4DGen remain unchanged. Additional visual results and raw vote counts are reported; these do not establish a same-metric performance improvement.

T1.justification: Appendix C newly formalizes the discrete spherical point set through icosahedral sampling and normalization, and states averaging as the closed-form fusion used for Equation 3. The original equations and objectives remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the first framework for 4K omnidirectional dynamic generation without annotated 4D training data, using panoramic denoising and geometry-regularized lifting for immersive exploration. The renamed lifting component and rewritten contribution bullets preserve this scope.

C2.justification: v3 newly characterizes the animation strategies as having similar visual quality in Table 2 and explains choosing circle-mode qualitative examples because the baseline modes perform similarly. The existing explanations of motion inconsistency, geometric degradation and flickering, together with all three stated limitations, are retained.

D1.justification: Appendices B–D add generator provenance, spherical discretization and fusion, mask construction, 14-frame and 25-step settings, and the 42-user questionnaire design and counts. Existing optimization budgets largely move from Section 4.1 to Appendix C. The project link disappears and a future code-release promise is added. Appendix C's W/4 perspective dimensions conflict with the retained 512×512 specification in Section 4.1.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations including Mixture of Diffusers, RoomDreamer, InstructLayout, Wonderworld and the new evaluation metrics, while dropping DreamSpace and PanoDiffusion. Descriptions of related scene-generation work are refined, but the central research positioning and novelty claim remain stable.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and substantial method prose are rewritten. Results are reorganized into quantitative and qualitative discussions, the lifting component is renamed, and implementation and ethics material is reorganized into new appendices. Citation style, headings and author information also change.

P2.justification: The single baseline example in v1 Figure 5 becomes a three-scene, two-view comparison in v3 Figure 4. The earlier fireworks visualization reappears within the expanded appendix Figure 7. Tables are restructured around new metrics and baseline configurations, and the document template and captions change; the ablation images are largely retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens assessment through broader image/video quality measurements and makes previously unspecified implementation and user-study details inspectable in Appendices B–D. These gains are tempered by conflicting perspective-resolution specifications and removal of the project link while code release remains prospective. Overall, the evidence and reproducibility documentation improve, but unresolved reporting issues limit the net gain.
